statement: All primes are written in order: \(p_1 = 2, p_2 = 3, p_3 = 5, \ldots\) Find all pairs of positive integers \(a, b\) with \(a - b \geq 2\) such that \(p_a - p_b\) divides \(2(a - b)\).

Let \(ABCD\) be a parallelogram with obtuse angle at \(A\). \(P\) is on segment \(BD\). The circle with center \(P\) passing through \(A\) meets line \(AD\) at \(A\) and \(Y\), and meets line \(AB\) at \(A\) and \(X\). Line \(AP\) meets \(BC\) at \(Q\) and \(CD\) at \(R\). Prove \(\angle XPY = \angle XQY + \angle XRY\).
What is the largest subset of \(\{1, 2, \ldots, 2013\}\) such that no three distinct elements \(a, b, c\) in the subset satisfy: \(a\) is a divisor or multiple of \(b - c\)?

An \(n \times n \times n\) cube is built from \(1 \times 1 \times 1\) unit cubes, colored black or white, such that every \(n \times 1 \times 1\), \(1 \times n \times 1\), and \(1 \times 1 \times n\) subprism has exactly two black cubes separated by an even number of white cubes. Show that half the black cubes can be recolored white so that each such subprism has exactly one black cube.

A pair of integers is special if it is of the form \((n, n-1)\) or \((n-1, n)\). Let \(n, m\) be positive integers with \((n, m)\) not special. Show \((n, m)\) can be expressed as a sum of two or more different special pairs if and only if \(n + m \geq (n - m)^2\).

Let \(A_1 A_2 \cdots A_8\) be a convex octagon with all sides equal and opposite sides parallel. For each \(i\), define \(B_i\) as the intersection of \(A_i A_{i+4}\) and \(A_{i-1} A_{i+1}\) (indices mod 8). Show that for some \(i \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}\): \(\dfrac{A_i A_{i+4}}{B_i B_{i+4}} \leq \dfrac{3}{2}\).
